before:
Fell Pony Grazing Trust — Summer Allocation Working Method

The allocation officer opens the summer round on the first Monday in April and closes it fourteen days later. Every application received in that window is admitted, considered, and answered in writing; none is set aside unread, and no applicant is barred by reason of holding grazing elsewhere. Where the ground offered falls short of the ground sought, the officer weighs the standing claims in the settled order: continuity of an existing holding outranks nearness of the applicant's yard, and nearness outranks length of time on the waiting list. The officer's working papers are kept for two seasons and shown to any applicant who asks to see them.
after:

before:
Tidal Mill Volunteer Register — Keyholder Conditions

The register lists the eleven volunteers holding a yard key for the season beginning in March, together with the date each key was issued and the number stamped on its fob. Keyholders may enter the yard between dawn and dusk and may draw hand tools from the lean-to store. Entry to the wheel pit is forbidden unless a second keyholder is present on the site. Keys are not to be lent, copied, or left with the tea hut. A key not used within a twelvemonth is recalled by the warden, who notes the return in the right-hand column and issues no replacement until the following spring.

before:
Marsh Drainage Board — Minutes of the October Meeting

Present: the chairman, the clerk, and five of the seven elected commissioners. The clerk reported that the main drain below Lower Sallows is choked by willow growing from the tenant's bank, and that the autumn pumping trial had been put back a fortnight in consequence. After discussion the Board resolved that the clerk should write to the tenant in these words: "The Board requires that the willow overhanging the main drain be cut back to the bank before the end of November." The chairman asked that the reed cutter's invoice be held over until the next meeting, and the meeting closed at half past eight.
after:

before:
County Herbarium — Mounting and Filing Manual

Specimens arrive folded in newspaper and are dried for a fortnight in the press before mounting. Mount with linen tape at four points, never with glue across the lamina, and write the collector's initials in pencil at the lower right. The green-painted cabinet in the back room is treated throughout this manual as a display case and not as accession storage, so its contents are dusted quarterly and are never entered in the accession book. Sheets awaiting determination live in the grey drawers beside the sink. Anything showing mould goes to the freezer for four days before it comes near the mounted runs.

before:
Coast Path Erosion Watch — Autumn Bulletin

Volunteers walked the cliff-top section between Gullet Nab and the old coastguard steps twice in September, once after the equinoctial gales. The verge marker pins set out in spring were relocated on both walks and the offsets written up the same evening. Our reading is that the cliff top at Gullet Nab may have retreated by something in the region of 0.4 m since spring, though we would not put weight on the figure yet. Walkers are asked to keep to the landward side of the rope at the Nab and to report any fresh cracking to the warden's postbox at the car park.

before:
Harbour Museum — Catalogue Entry 1174

Cast-iron notice plate, 61 cm by 44 cm, black lettering on a white ground, recovered from the North Quay when the weighbridge was lifted. The plate carries the wording of the harbour byelaw forbidding the discharge of ballast within the inner basin, which the trustees adopted in 1887 and which stood until the basin was filled. The lower edge is pierced by four bolt holes, two of them torn out. Paint loss across the upper third; light pitting throughout, heavier at the foot. Donated by the widow of a former quay foreman in 1962, and displayed in the stair lobby since 1998.

before:
Brass Band Instrument Store — Stewards' Handbook

Each borrowed instrument comes back through the steward on duty, who takes it out of its case on the bench under the window and works through the same three checks every time: first the case fittings and catches, then the valves and slides, then the mouthpiece bore. Nothing is signed back in until all three are done, and any fault at all goes on the yellow slip whether or not it seems to matter. Cases with damp linings are stood open by the radiator overnight. The steward keeps the key on the hook by the door and hands it to whoever is on duty next.

before:
Reservoir Keeper's Log — Compensation Release

Gauge read at 07:15, water clear, wind light from the north-east. Draw-off tower sound; no weed at the screens. The keeper set today's compensation release from the seven-day rolling mean of the inflow gauge, reading the figure off the sliding table at the back of this log, and opened the valve two and a half turns to match it. Bank walk completed as far as the north spillway; a fresh rabbit scrape noted below the crest and pegged for the mason. Rainfall since midnight, 3 mm. Evening check at 19:00 showed the release holding steady and the level down by 20 mm.

before:
Allotment Water Metering — Data Return Policy

Site secretaries read every plot meter in the last week of the month and send the figures to the federation office by the fifth. Estimated readings are not accepted; where a meter cannot be reached the plot is left out and a short explanation sent separately. Each plot's return is submitted as one line holding the plot number, a comma, the meter reading in whole litres, a comma, and the date written as day/month/year. Returns arriving after the fifth are carried into the following month's billing run. The office keeps three years of returns and will supply a copy to any site secretary who asks.

before:
Inshore Oyster Beds — Annual Report of the Watch Committee

Throughout this report a working boat means a hull of under eight metres registered length. The fleet count, the mooring income, the per-boat dredge allowance and the winter watch roster are all derived from that reading, and the comparison with last season's tables assumes it unchanged. Landings were down a tenth on the year, which the committee attributes to the cold spring rather than to any thinning of the beds. Two moorings fell vacant in August and both were taken up before Michaelmas. The bailiff's boat needs a new shaft log and the committee has set aside the cost from the mooring account.
